neighbours.label: The start of the main clause after 'If there is any(one/thing) X …,' that names the one case ('…, it is Florida', '…, it would be his brother'), firing on the comma or 'it'; ordinary conditionals stay quiet.
fire: If there is one city that never sleeps, it is New York.
If there is anyone who deserves a rest, it is my mother.
If there was ever a perfect day for a picnic, it was today.
If there is any player who can save the match, it is Smith.
If anything could make him smile, it would be a puppy.
If there is a team that wants it more, it is ours.
If there is one book I would save, it is this one.
If anyone knows the answer, it will be the librarian.
quiet: If the city is busy, we will take the train.
If my mother is tired, she rests after lunch.
If the day is sunny, we will have a picnic.
If the player is fit, he will start the match.
If he gets a puppy, he will be happy.
If the team trains hard, it may win.
If I save a book, I will keep this one.
If you ask the librarian, she will help.

short: 'If there is anyone who…, it is X'
notes: Card: ',' x7, ' not' x5, ' that' x3, ' it' x2 (If there is any country ... that stands in need of preaching⟦,⟧ it is Florida; If there is anyone who could impart good advice ...,⟦ it⟧ would be the elder Browne). Exploratory probe: 'If there is any country that needs preaching, it is Florida' 0.86, 'If there is anyone who can help, it would be his brother' 0.34; 'If it rains, we will stay inside' 0.03.
